DELETE /api/profile/image.summary: Remove the caller's own profile picture.
DELETE /api/profile/image.description:
Deletes the stored bytes as well as the row — one of the three destructive routes
that satisfy a GDPR Art. 17 erasure request (the others being the replace half of POST and the account
delete's cascade).

Its rate limit is a SEPARATE budget from the upload's: sharing one would mean a user who has exhausted
it uploading could not remove their picture, which throttles the erasure control itself.

GET /api/accounts/net-worth-history.summary: Net worth over time, reconstructed from stored data.
GET /api/accounts/net-worth-history.description:
Rebuilds the series on read from transactions, account estimates, property
                        estimates and exchange rates, with every point measured as of that point's own
                        instant. Property value is included only for a caller holding both
                        properties.read and properties.estimates.read (propertiesIncluded), and a
                        property counts only while held — from acquisition until disposal. Nothing is
                        interpolated and no past point is scaled by the present figure, so the line can
                        fall and can go negative.

                        A point covers [periodStart, nextPeriodStart) and is DATED AT ITS PERIOD END —
                        the instant it describes. Net worth is a stock, not a flow. A point covering
                        October 2024 is dated 2024-11-01.

                        A point whose figure is understated (an account had no rate then) says so with
                        unconvertedAccountCount; one that stepped because an estimate took effect says
                        so with revaluedAccountCount. Neither is smoothed and neither is a failure.

                        An empty series always carries an emptyReason naming the cause — including a
                        window that ends before the first account was opened, which is a 200, not a
                        400. from/to are ISO-8601 dates (yyyy-MM-dd).

                        MEMBERSHIP IS THE OPEN/CLOSED TERM, PER POINT: an account counts at a point
                        when it had opened before that point's instant and had not closed by it.
                        Archiving is a list filter and has no bearing on any figure here, so filing an
                        account away never moves the line. Because both endpoints evaluate that one
                        rule, the final point still equals GET /accounts/totals exactly — now
                        structurally rather than by two predicates being kept in step.

GET /api/accounts/summary.summary: Summary rollup: counts by status and type, the value aggregates and the per-account allocations.
GET /api/accounts/summary.description: Aggregated server-side so the page header and its allocation donuts do not have to fetch every account.

GET /api/accounts/totals.summary: Get total assets, liabilities and net worth in the main currency.
GET /api/accounts/totals.description:
Converts each in-term account's balance — and, for a caller holding both
                        properties.read and properties.estimates.read, the in-force estimate of each
                        property held now — into the main currency using the rate in force now, and
                        returns total assets (property value included), total liabilities, net worth,
                        the property value on its own line, and the accounts and properties that could
                        not be converted (no rate to the main currency). allocations lists every
                        contributing account and property with its converted, signed contribution, so
                        the rows sum to net worth. propertiesIncluded says which of the two figures
                        this is; it depends on the caller's claims alone.
                        Everything is measured as of now, exclusively: a transaction, rate, estimate or
                        account dated in the future does not count. An unsupported or archived
                        mainCurrency is rejected with 400.

                        MEMBERSHIP IS THE OPEN/CLOSED TERM: an account counts when it opened before now
                        and has not closed by it. Archiving an account does NOT change this figure —
                        it controls only what appears in lists. Closing one does, from its close date
                        onward.

parameters.name: mainCurrency
parameters.description: The currency to convert into. Defaults to NOK.

Omit all filters to export everything; pass the page's current filter state to export exactly the filtered set.

The exported card carries the contact's names, aliases
(including maiden and former names, with their free-text labels), middle name, dates of birth and

Embed each contact's image. Opt-in, default false.

404 when the contact does not exist, has no image, or its stored content type is

GET /api/contacts/{id}/conversion-previe.summary: Preview converting a contact between Person and Organization.
GET /api/contacts/{id}/conversion-previe.description:
A read-only dry run (issue #335): the derived target details, the fields that
would be lost or carried over, the contact-method labels that would clamp to Other, and any blockers.
Writes nothing. Echo updatedAt as expectedUpdatedAt on the conversion. Needs contacts.read and
contacts.update; blocker photo ids need photos.read and property names properties.read.

GET /api/contacts/{id}/vcard.summary: Export a single contact as an RFC 6350 vCard 4.0 .vcf file.
GET /api/contacts/{id}/vcard.description:
The exported card carries the contact's names, aliases
(including maiden and former names, with their free-text labels), middle name, dates of birth and
death, an organization's establishment and dissolution dates, the archive date, addresses
(with each geocoded address's coordinates and time zone), email addresses, phone numbers and notes.

parameters.name: includeImages
parameters.description:
Embed the contact's image as a PHOTO (person) or
LOGO (organization) data URI. Opt-in and default false on BOTH export endpoints: flipping the
single-contact default would silently change what an existing caller receives from a shipped endpoint.

GET /api/contract-limits.summary: The effective per-contract limits for the Contracts page.

GET /api/contracts.summary: List contracts (lean projection with derived status), with search, filtering, sorting and pagination.
GET /api/contracts.description:
'search' matches the name, the description, the reference number and linked contact-party
                        names (case-insensitive substring). 'sortBy' accepts Name (default), StartDate, EndDate,
                        Type, Status and ReferenceNumber; ReferenceNumber sorts ascending by default with
                        contracts that have none last in both directions (issue #181).

GET /api/contracts/summary.summary: Summary rollup: counts by status and by type, the run rate, and the derived upcoming movements.
GET /api/contracts/summary.description:
The run rate is direction-aware (issue #159): 'monthly'/'yearly'/'byType' are the
                        OUTGOING side and keep their pre-#159 meaning, 'incomingMonthly'/'incomingYearly'/
                        'incomingByType' are the incoming side, and 'netMonthly'/'netYearly' are incoming
                        minus outgoing — the only signed figures in the payload. No gross ever mixes the
                        two. A gross is null when its own side has nothing convertible; the net is null
                        only when both are. One base currency is elected from both directions, and a
                        currency with no rate to it is named in 'unconvertedCurrencies' and excluded from
                        both sides and the net rather than folded in at 1:1.

GET /api/contracts/{contractId}/smart-ta.summary: List the transactions a contract's smart tags match.
GET /api/contracts/{contractId}/smart-ta.description:
A transaction matches when it carries one of the contract's smart tags, is dated
                        inside the contract's term, and its merchant is a contact party on the contract.
                        Paged, searchable and sortable with the transaction list's keys. The summary
                        totals the whole matched set per currency, independent of search and paging.
                        A structurally empty result is a 200 with scope.emptyReason set.

GET /api/contracts/{contractId}/smart-ta.summary: Get the smart tags configured for a contract.
GET /api/contracts/{contractId}/smart-ta.description:
Lists the transaction tags currently associated with the contract as smart
                        tags, oldest association first. An empty list is a healthy 200, never a 404.

GET /api/contracts/{id}.summary: Get one contract with minimal party/file references and derived status.

GET /api/contracts/{id}/events.summary: List a contract's events, with search, type/date filters, sorting and pagination.
GET /api/contracts/{id}/events.description:
Newest first by default. The search term spans the title, the description AND
                        the notes: all three sit behind contracts.read and are returned to the same
                        callers, so the notes field being absent from the timeline is a presentation
                        rule and never an access one. Events are NOT inlined on GET /api/contracts/{id}
                        — an event log grows without bound, so it is paged on its own route.

GET /api/contracts/{id}/files.summary: List the documents attached to a contract.
GET /api/contracts/{id}/files.description: Unpaged and bounded by the per-contract file cap. A contract with no documents returns an empty array, never a 404.

GET /api/contracts/{id}/files/{fileId}.summary: Download a document attached to a contract.

GET /api/contracts/{id}/terms.summary: Get the term (rate/fee) history for a contract.
GET /api/contracts/{id}/terms.description:
Lists the full term history for the contract, newest effective date first.
                        Optionally filtered by an as-of date. An archived contract's history stays
                        readable.

GET /api/contracts/{id}/terms/current.summary: Get the currently-effective term of each series on a contract.
GET /api/contracts/{id}/terms/current.description:
Returns the in-force entry of each labelled series that has at least one
                        entry, as of now or the supplied as-of date. An empty array is a healthy
                        response — a contract with no recorded price is not a defect.

GET /api/currencies.description:
List currencies with search, sorting and pagination. Every row carries its derived
                        status (Synced, FetchingHistory, NoLongerPublished, SyncingOff, NotPublished,
                        Archived), which statuses= filters and sortBy=status orders, for every caller.
                        A caller holding system-settings.read also gets each non-archived row's
                        exchange-rate sync projection (sync). status=active|archived is the older
                        archival filter, kept for the currency pickers.

parameters.name: code
parameters.description: The code for the currency to get.

GET /api/exchange-rates.description: List exchange rates with search, sorting and pagination.

GET /api/exchange-rates/latest.summary: Get the latest rate for a currency pair.
GET /api/exchange-rates/latest.description: Returns the newest row in force for from -> to: a stored from -> to row, or a fetched to -> from row returned as its inverse. An inverted response has inverted = true, the codes swapped and rate = 1 / the stored rate, unrounded, so it can carry more than 8 decimals (a JavaScript Number keeps about 15-17 significant digits). Its exchangeRateId, asOf, createdAt and updatedAt are the STORED row's, so GET /api/exchange-rates/{id} with that id returns the to -> from row; a caller that follows ids must check inverted. No NOK hop: use /api/exchange-rates/resolved for the rate a conversion would use. 400 for a code that is not exactly three letters; 404 when nothing is in force, a currency does not exist, or from equals to.

GET /api/exchange-rates/resolved.summary: Get the rate a conversion would use right now, and how it was built.
GET /api/exchange-rates/resolved.description: The same resolution the account totals use: a direct row, a fetched reverse row inverted, or a hop through NOK (method 0 SameCurrency, 1 Direct, 2 Inverted, 3 ViaNok). Each leg is shown in the logical direction with the rate actually multiplied in; its exchangeRateId names the stored row, whose own pair is the reverse when inverted is true. Rates are unrounded and can carry more than 8 decimals (a JavaScript Number keeps about 15-17 significant digits). asOf is the older leg's date for a hop. 400 for a code that is not exactly three letters; 404 when a currency does not exist or nothing resolves.

GET /api/exchange-rates/summary.summary: Counts by status and source, the currencies in use and the attribution.

GET /api/exchange-rates/{id}.summary: Get a single exchange rate record.

parameters.name: id

GET /api/news-articles/{id}/revisions.summary: An article's earlier versions, newest first, metadata only.

GET /api/news-articles/{id}/revisions/{n.summary: One earlier version with its body.

GET /api/news-feeds.summary: List news feeds by state, derived health, tag and search.

GET /api/news-feeds/catalogue.summary: Every feed not pending deletion, unpaged and with no URL.

GET /api/news-feeds/opml.summary: Export every feed not pending deletion as an OPML 2.0 file, each tag a folder.

GET /api/news-feeds/unread-counts.summary: Unread counts in total, by feed and by effective tag; archived feeds excluded.

GET /api/news-status.summary: News storage state, totals against the resolved quotas, and the feeds using the most image bytes.

GET /api/news-tags.summary: List news tags with search, archival-status filter, sort and paging.

GET /api/photo-tags.summary: List photo tags with search, archival-status filter, sort and paging.

GET /api/photos.summary: List photos with search, tag/person/album/date-range filters, sort and paging.

GET /api/photos/stats.summary: Aggregate library counts (total, favourites, per-tag, per-person) for the Overview panel.

GET /api/photos/{id}.summary: Get a photo with its tag/person/album link IDs and extracted metadata.

GET /api/photos/{id}/content.summary: Stream a photo's original from the object store.
GET /api/photos/{id}/content.description:
Served inline under photos.read with nosniff, CORP same-site, a strong ETag (the SHA-256) and range
processing; private, no-cache, so revalidation costs one 304 with no body (issue #428 §5.2).

GET /api/photos/{id}/thumbnail.summary: Stream a photo's WebP thumbnail (Small 200 px or Medium 400 px).
GET /api/photos/{id}/thumbnail.description:
404 photo-thumbnail-not-found for an unknown photo, a thumbnail not ready yet and a released one
alike. Served inline with a strong ETag and private, no-cache, so revalidation costs one 304 with no body.

GET /api/podcast-artwork/{id}/content.summary: Podcast artwork: Small, Medium (default) or the stored Original.

GET /api/podcast-episodes.summary: One page of episodes of podcast feeds, newest or oldest first; continue with nextCursor.

GET /api/podcast-episodes/{id}.summary: One episode with its description, show notes and chapters.

GET /api/podcast-episodes/{id}/audio/con.summary: An episode's stored audio as an attachment, with nosniff, CORP same-site, a strong ETag and range processing.

GET /api/profile.summary: Read the current user's own profile and its completeness flag.

GET /api/profile-images/{userId}.description:
Gated on profile-images.read, which every role holds — revoking it from a role is
the supported way to narrow who sees colleagues' pictures.

404 — with a body naming no identifier — when the user does not exist, has no picture, is
administratively disabled, or the stored content type is not a permitted profile picture. The '?v='
parameter is a cache key only and is never bound or parsed. Served inline with a strong ETag and
no-cache, so a removed picture 404s on the next revalidation rather than hiding behind a cached 200.

GET /api/properties.description:
List properties with search, subtype and status filters, sorting and pagination.
                        sortBy=value orders by the estimate in force now, in each property's own
                        currency WITHOUT conversion (a mixed-currency list sorts by raw magnitude),
                        with properties that have no estimate last in both directions.

GET /api/properties/summary.description:
Counts by type (unarchived only) and by derived status. For a caller holding
                        properties.estimates.read, also the in-force estimates of the owned properties
                        summed per currency, and a total converted to baseCurrency at the latest rate;
                        a currency with no rate is named in unconvertedCurrencies and left out of the
                        total. Blank baseCurrency picks the currency most owned properties use.

GET /api/properties/{id}.summary: Get a property, with its detail sub-object.

GET /api/properties/{propertyId}/contrac.summary: Get the contracts that name a property as a party.
GET /api/properties/{propertyId}/contrac.description:
One row per contract, with every role the property holds on it. Requires both
                        properties.read and contracts.read: the rows name contracts, which
                        properties.read alone does not license.

GET /api/properties/{propertyId}/estimat.summary: Get the estimated-value history for a property.
GET /api/properties/{propertyId}/estimat.description:
Lists the full estimate history for the property, newest effective date first.
                        Optionally cut off at an as-of date.

GET /api/properties/{propertyId}/estimat.summary: Get the currently-effective estimated value for a property.
GET /api/properties/{propertyId}/estimat.description:
Returns the in-force estimate as of now or the supplied as-of date, or a null
                        body when the property has no estimate in force.

GET /api/properties/{propertyId}/events.summary: List a property's events, with search, type/date/source filters, sorting and pagination.
GET /api/properties/{propertyId}/events.description:
Newest first by default. The search term spans the title, the description AND
                        the notes. Events are NOT inlined on GET /api/properties/{id}.

GET /api/properties/{propertyId}/files.summary: List the documents attached to a property.
GET /api/properties/{propertyId}/files.description:
Unpaged and uncapped, oldest attachment first; metadata only. A property with no
                        documents returns an empty array, never a 404. issuedBy is the contact id only.

GET /api/properties/{propertyId}/files/{.summary: Download a document attached to a property.

GET /api/properties/{propertyId}/smart-t.summary: Get the smart tags configured for a property.
GET /api/properties/{propertyId}/smart-t.description:
Lists the transaction tags currently associated with the property as smart
                        tags, oldest association first. An empty list is a healthy 200, never a 404.

GET /api/property-limits.summary: The effective per-property limits for the Properties page.

GET /api/recipe-tags.summary: List recipe tags; an omitted status returns active and archived tags.

GET /api/recipes.summary: List recipes with search (title or ingredient), tag, time, photo, file and status filters, sort and paging.

GET /api/recipes/{id}.summary: Get a recipe, optionally with its amounts scaled to ?servings= (read-only, nothing is stored).

GET /api/recurrence-patterns.summary: List recurrence patterns, optionally filtered by calendar.

GET /api/recurrence-patterns/{id}/events.summary: List all generated events (past and future) for a recurrence pattern, paged.

GET /api/recurrence-patterns/{id}/ics.summary: Export a recurring series as one RRULE VEVENT (or its per-occurrence fallback).

GET /api/recurrence-patterns/{id}/ics/su.summary: Summarize what a recurring series' .ics export would contain.

GET /api/system-settings/exchange-rate-s.summary: Every currency with its sync configuration.
The sync's state, schedule and last run.

GET /api/system-settings/instrument-pric.summary: The registered price sources, their state and the sync status. Empty while no source is installed.

GET /api/task-tags.summary: List task tags (search, status filter, sort, paginate).

GET /api/tasks/ics.summary: Export the current filtered task view as an RFC 5545 VTODO .ics file, attached files inline.

GET /api/tasks/ics/summary.summary: Summarize what a VTODO .ics export of the filtered task view would contain.

GET /api/tasks/{id}.summary: Get a task with its tag IDs and attachment metadata.

GET /api/tax-statements/summary.summary: Summary rollup: years on file, the fiscal-year bounds and the per-year declared figures.

GET /api/tax-statements/{id}.summary: Get a tax statement with its selected tag IDs and file metadata.

GET /api/tax-statements/{id}/files/{file.summary: Download an attached tax statement document.

GET /api/tax-statements/{id}/report.summary: Get the reconciliation report (declared vs. derived figures and diffs).

GET /api/transaction-tags.description: List transaction tags with search, status filter, sorting and pagination.

GET /api/transaction-tags/{id}.summary: Get a transaction tag based on the transaction tag ID.
GET /api/transaction-tags/{id}.description: Get a transaction tag based on the transaction tag ID.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The ID for the transaction tag to get.

GET /api/transactions.description: List transactions with search, filtering, sorting and pagination.

GET /api/transactions/summary.summary: Summary rollup: counts by status and direction, plus the money in / out totals.
GET /api/transactions/summary.description: Aggregated server-side over every transaction, so the page header does not have to fetch the ledger to count it.

GET /api/transactions/{id}.summary: Get a transaction based on the transaction ID.
GET /api/transactions/{id}.description: Get a transaction based on the transaction ID.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The ID for the transaction to get.

GET /api/transactions/{transactionId}/fi.summary: Get files attached to a transaction.
GET /api/transactions/{transactionId}/fi.description: Get files attached to a transaction.

parameters.name: transactionId
parameters.description: The ID for the transaction.

GET /api/upload-limits.summary: The effective maximum upload size for file-upload surfaces.

GET /api/user-preferences/{pageKey}.summary: Get user preference for page key.
GET /api/user-preferences/{pageKey}.description: Get user preference for page key.

parameters.name: pageKey
parameters.description: The page key for the preference to get.

GET /api/weather/current.summary: The current conditions and today's summary for a place.

GET /api/weather/daily.summary: Day summaries over a range of at most 366 days; days with no data are omitted.

GET /api/weather/hourly.summary: The effective forecast steps in a window of at most 10 days (fromUtc/toUtc), or of one point-local day (date).

GET /api/weather/points.summary: Every weather point, paged; sortBy=LinkedLocationCount needs locations.read.

GET /api/weather/points/options.summary: The weather points a user can pick, by name — or nearest first from nearLocationId (needs locations.read).

GET /api/weather/points/{weatherPointId}.summary: The places that use a weather point: id, name and whole-km distance only.

GET /api/weather/preferences.summary: The caller's own weather place, and the household default.

PATCH /api/tax-statements/{id}/status.summary: Set the review status and optional status comment; stamps StatusChangedAt.

POST /api/account/email.summary: Request a change of the signed-in user's email address.

POST /api/account/password.summary: Change the signed-in user's own password.

POST /api/accounts.description:
Create a new account. If a new account is created, the url for the new account is 
                        returned in the location header.

POST /api/accounts/{accountId}/estimates.summary: Create a new estimated-value entry on an account.

POST /api/accounts/{accountId}/files.summary: Attach an uploaded file to an account (requires accounts.update + files.read).

POST /api/accounts/{accountId}/files/{fi.summary: Queue AI analysis of an account statement file.
POST /api/accounts/{accountId}/files/{fi.description: Records the consent and queues the analysis; the worker sends the file and extracts candidate transactions. Answers 202 with the job id; poll GET /api/file-analysis/{id}. 409 analysis_in_progress carries the open job's id. File type must be Statement.

POST /api/accounts/{accountId}/smart-tag.summary: Associate an existing tag with an account as a smart tag.

POST /api/albums.summary: Create an album with optional initial member photos.

POST /api/book-tags.summary: Create a book tag; a name colliding with an existing (incl. archived) tag returns 409.

POST /api/books.summary: Create a book. Links are scalar ids; each non-empty array needs its read claim.

POST /api/budget-items.description:
Create a new budget item. A budget item is a planned amount for a transaction tag, so 
                        transactionTagId is required: a missing, empty, unknown or archived tag is a 400, and a tag 
                        already planned for in the target budget is a 409. If a new budget item is created, the url 
                        for the new budget item is returned in the location header.

POST /api/budgets.description:
Create a new budget. If a new budget is created, the url for the new budget is 
                        returned in the location header.

POST /api/calendars/{id}/ics.summary: Import an RFC 5545 .ics file into an existing calendar.

POST /api/contacts/vcard.summary: Import an RFC 6350 vCard 4.0 .vcf file, creating or updating contacts matched by ExternalUid.

POST /api/contacts/{contactId}/aliases.summary: Add one alternative name to a contact.
POST /api/contacts/{contactId}/aliases.description:
409 when the contact already carries that value (compared case- AND
accent-insensitively, on the value alone — two labels cannot smuggle in a second "Hansen"); 422 when
the contact is already at its 32-alias cap. Both name the field `value` in the problem-details
`errors` dictionary, and neither echoes the submitted value or label.

POST /api/contacts/{id}/avatar.summary: Attach or replace a contact's image.
POST /api/contacts/{id}/avatar.description:
Takes the image BYTES as multipart/form-data under the part name 'file' — never a
fileId. A caller-supplied id would let a contacts.update holder point a contact at any row in the file
store and read its bytes back through the contacts.read-gated endpoint above.

The bytes are validated against a narrower allow-list than a general upload (PNG, JPEG or WebP; magic
bytes checked; at most 1024 x 1024; not animated), stripped of all embedded metadata and re-validated
before storage. The previous image's file is released in the SAME transaction.

POST /api/contacts/{id}/conversion.summary: Convert a contact between Person and Organization.
POST /api/contacts/{id}/conversion.description:
Converts the contact in one transaction, deriving the target details from the
stored row (issue #335); its id and its links are kept. 409 with code contact-conversion-stale when
expectedUpdatedAt no longer matches, or contact-type-change-blocked while a photo person tag (to
Organization) or a homeowner-association link (to Person) exists. 422 for the current type, or for a
derived name that needs an override.

POST /api/contracts/{contractId}/smart-t.summary: Associate an existing tag with a contract as a smart tag.

POST /api/contracts/{id}/events.summary: Record one event on a contract.
POST /api/contracts/{id}/events.description:
createdBy and createdAtUtc are server-stamped and ignored if present in the
                        body. occurredAt must not be in the future — a 60-second forward tolerance
                        allows for a client clock that runs slightly fast, and beyond that the request
                        is a 400 keyed to the field. Writing to an archived contract is permitted,
                        matching the party, term and file writes.

POST /api/contracts/{id}/files.summary: Attach an already-uploaded document to a contract (requires contracts.update + files.read).

POST /api/contracts/{id}/parties.summary: Add a party in a role, optionally for a term (exactly one of accountId/contactId).

POST /api/contracts/{id}/terms.summary: Create a term (rate/fee) entry on a contract.
POST /api/contracts/{id}/terms.description:
Every term is a labelled series; 'label' names what it prices. A money-valued
                        term must name its currency — a contract has none of its own to default from.
                        'direction' says which way the money moves from the household's perspective;
                        it is optional, omitting it means Outgoing, and every unit accepts either.

POST /api/exchange-rates.summary: Add a new exchange rate. To correct an existing entry, use PUT instead.

POST /api/file-analysis/{analysisJobId}/.summary: Import selected candidate transactions from an analysis job.
POST /api/file-analysis/{analysisJobId}/.description: Commits the specified candidates as real transactions. Optional field overrides (date, description, amount, currency) are applied before import. Each candidate is validated like any other transaction write: its currency must be the account's, its contact and tags must exist and be active, and a candidate that is no longer Pending is reported as a failure rather than imported again. A closed or archived account refuses the whole request (400); a candidate reviewed by a concurrent request is a 409.

parameters.name: analysisJobId
parameters.description: Analysis Job ID

POST /api/file-analysis/{analysisJobId}/.summary: Run (or re-run) the AI match step for an extraction-completed analysis job.
POST /api/file-analysis/{analysisJobId}/.description: Sends the user's active contacts (names, and aliases when the job's consent covers them) and tags (names, and descriptions likewise) to the AI provider to resolve each candidate's merchant/category, persists the matches, and returns the updated job. Synchronous. A provider failure is recorded on matchStatus and never blocks importing the candidates. 409 with code file_analysis_destination_changed when the provider settings changed since the analysis.

parameters.name: analysisJobId
parameters.description: Analysis Job ID

POST /api/files.description:
Upload a file with optional description. Returns file metadata. 'area' (Finance, Journal or Library) is
required and only decides which folder on the file store holds the bytes (issue #448); it never affects who may read or
link the file. There is no contacts area here: contact images go through the avatar endpoint.

POST /api/journal-entries/vjournal.summary: Import an RFC 5545 VJOURNAL .ics file into the shared journal-entries board.

POST /api/legal/respond.summary: Accept or decline the License or the current Terms of Service.

POST /api/legal/terms-of-service/version.summary: Publish a new current Terms of Service version; prior versions are retained untouched.

POST /api/locations/search.summary: Search an address or place name: Kartverket for Norway, Open-Meteo for the rest of the world.

POST /api/locations/{sourceId}/merge.summary: Merge a location into another; returns the surviving target.

POST /api/news-articles/mark-read.summary: Mark read what the list's filters match, up to the first page's asOfUtc; repeat while hasMore.

POST /api/news-articles/read-state.summary: Set one read state on 1–500 articles; unknown ids change nothing.

POST /api/news-feeds.summary: Subscribe to a feed. No outbound request is made; the worker fetches it on its next tick.

POST /api/news-feeds/opml.summary: Subscribe to the feeds of an OPML file in one step and report each. No outbound request is made.

POST /api/news-feeds/opml/export.summary: Export the named feeds as an OPML 2.0 file; unknown ids and feeds pending deletion are skipped.

POST /api/news-feeds/{id}/archive.summary: Archive a feed: it stops being fetched and leaves the default lists.

POST /api/news-feeds/{id}/refresh.summary: Ask the worker to fetch the feed soon (no sooner than 60 s after its last attempt).

POST /api/news-feeds/{id}/release-quaran.summary: Release a quarantined feed so the worker fetches it again.

POST /api/photo-tags.summary: Create a photo tag; a name colliding with an existing (incl. archived) tag returns 409.

POST /api/photos.summary: Upload a photo: writes the original to the photo store and creates the library photo.
POST /api/photos.description:
multipart/form-data: the image as part 'file', plus the optional NewPhotoUpload fields. Runs
EXIF/IPTC/XMP extraction. 409 photo-duplicate when the same bytes are already a photo (issue #428 §5.1).

POST /api/podcast-episodes/{id}/audio.summary: Queue a server download of the episode's audio. No body; already stored is a 200.

POST /api/profile/image.summary: Attach or replace the caller's own profile picture.
POST /api/profile/image.description:
Takes the image BYTES as multipart/form-data under the part name 'file' — never a
fileId. A caller-supplied id would let a self-service write point an identity row at arbitrary stored
bytes and read them back through the authenticated read, an arbitrary-file-read primitive from two
innocuous capabilities.

There is no user id in the route or the body: this always writes the caller's own row.

Returns 200 with the new ImageVersion — not 204, because the client needs the token to re-key the
image URL. The bytes are validated against a narrow allow-list (PNG, JPEG or WebP; magic bytes checked;
at most 1024 x 1024; not animated), stripped of all embedded metadata and re-validated before storage.

POST /api/properties.description: Creates a property with exactly one detail sub-object matching its type.

POST /api/properties/{propertyId}/estima.summary: Record a new estimated-value entry on a property.

POST /api/properties/{propertyId}/events.summary: Record one event on a property.
POST /api/properties/{propertyId}/events.description:
source, createdBy and createdAtUtc are server-stamped and ignored if present in
                        the body. occurredAt more than 60 seconds ahead of the server clock is a 422
                        keyed occurredAt. A type illegal for the property's type, or one only the server
                        records (Archived, Unarchived, AcquisitionDateCleared, DisposalReversed), is a
                        422 keyed type.

POST /api/properties/{propertyId}/files.summary: Attach an already-uploaded document to a property (requires properties.update + files.read).
POST /api/properties/{propertyId}/files.description:
files.read is required because attaching makes the file's bytes downloadable
                        through properties.read. The file's server-recorded content type must be PDF,
                        PNG, JPEG or WebP. There is no per-property document cap.

POST /api/properties/{propertyId}/smart-.summary: Associate an existing tag with a property as a smart tag.

POST /api/recipe-tags.summary: Create a recipe tag; a name colliding with any existing tag (incl. archived) returns 409.

POST /api/recipes.summary: Create a recipe. Linking photos needs photos.read; linking files, files.read; linking tags, recipes.tags.read.

POST /api/recurrence-patterns.summary: Create a recurring event series; eagerly generates its bounded set of CalendarEvent occurrences in one transaction.

POST /api/recurrence-patterns/{id}/previ.summary: Preview a series edit: the overrides and exclusions it would drop, without saving.

POST /api/system-settings/exchange-rate-.summary: Fetch the provider's currency list, then read the status.

POST /api/tasks/ics.summary: Import an RFC 5545 VTODO .ics file into the shared task board.

POST /api/tax-statements/{id}/files.summary: Attach an already-uploaded document to a tax statement (requires taxes.update + files.read).

POST /api/transaction-tags.description:
Create a new transaction tag. If a new transaction tag is created, the url for the new transaction tag is
                        returned in the location header.

POST /api/transactions.description:
Create a new transaction. If a new transaction is created, the url for the new transaction is 
                        returned in the location header.

POST /api/transactions/{transactionId}/f.summary: Attach an uploaded file to a transaction (requires transactions.update + files.read).
POST /api/transactions/{transactionId}/f.description: Attach an already-uploaded file to a transaction.

parameters.name: transactionId
parameters.description: The ID for the transaction.

POST /api/weather/points.summary: Create a weather point from coordinates, or by copying a reviewed place's position. Links nothing.

POST /api/weather/points/{weatherPointId.summary: Fetch the forecast now, still honouring MET's expiry and any pause.

POST /logout.summary: Sign the current user out, clearing the authentication cookie.

PUT /api/accounts/{accountId}/estimates/.summary: Update an estimated-value entry on an account.

PUT /api/accounts/{accountId}/files/{fil.summary: Update an attached file's document type.

PUT /api/accounts/{id}.summary: Update the details for an account.
PUT /api/accounts/{id}.description:
Update the details for an account. If the account ID does not exist, the account is
                        created UNDER THAT ID and 201 is returned with its url in the location header, so a
                        retried PUT updates the same row rather than creating a second one. Creating needs
                        accounts.create in addition to accounts.update; without it an unknown ID is a 403.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The ID for the account to update.

PUT /api/albums/{id}.summary: Update an album: rename/describe, replace ordered membership, set cover, archive.

PUT /api/book-tags/{id}.summary: Update a book tag and toggle its archival state.

PUT /api/books/{id}.summary: Replace a book (not an upsert). version must match; a null array leaves that set unchanged.

PUT /api/budget-items/{id}.summary: Update the details for a budget item.
PUT /api/budget-items/{id}.description:
Update the details for a budget item. Not an upsert: an unknown ID is a 404 and
                        nothing is created. Use POST to create.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The ID for the budget item to update.

PUT /api/budgets/{id}.summary: Update the details for a budget.
PUT /api/budgets/{id}.description:
Update the details for a budget. Not an upsert: an unknown ID is a 404 and
                        nothing is created. Use POST to create.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The ID for the budget to update.

PUT /api/calendar-events/{id}.summary: Update this occurrence only; on a series row it becomes an override that a series edit keeps. Times are wall-clock in timeZoneId. RecurrencePatternId is immutable — use PUT /api/recurrence-patterns/{id} to edit a series.

PUT /api/calendars/{id}.summary: Rename, redescribe or recolour a calendar.

PUT /api/contacts/{contactId}/aliases/{a.summary: Replace one of a contact's alternative names.
PUT /api/contacts/{contactId}/aliases/{a.description:
A replace, not a patch: an omitted or blank `label` CLEARS a previously-set
one, matching the sibling sub-resources. There is deliberately no 422 here — a replace cannot grow the
collection, so the cap is unreachable on this verb.

PUT /api/contacts/{id}.summary: Update the details for a contact.
PUT /api/contacts/{id}.description:
Update the details for a contact. Not an upsert: an unknown ID is a 404 and
                        nothing is created. Use POST to create. A changed Type converts the contact
                        with the supplied details; 409 (code contact-type-change-blocked) while the
                        contact is tagged as a person on a photo (to Organization) or is a property's
                        homeowner association (to Person). 422 when a contact-method label is out of
                        scope for the type.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The ID for the contact to update.

PUT /api/contracts/{id}.summary: Update a contract's fields, including its archive and pause state (no dedicated archive or pause endpoint).
PUT /api/contracts/{id}.description:
422 when the requested type would leave an existing party holding a role that type
rejects (issue #157). The body names each offending party by id, role and display name, and nothing is
written — re-role those parties or detach them first.

Full replacement: every field is replaced, and an omitted or null field is cleared. That includes the
smart-tag scope (issue #308) — an omitted or null smartTagScopeStart / smartTagScopeEnd OPENS that side
of the scope, widening a narrowed one, so a caller rebuilding this body from a loaded contract must carry
both forward. Send each scope date as a calendar day with no offset ("2027-06-30") or as UTC midnight
("2027-06-30T00:00:00Z"); a value with an offset is converted to UTC before the time of day is dropped.
400 when a scope date falls outside 1900-01-01…9999-12-31; 422 (errors.smartTagScopeEnd) when the scope
ends before it starts.

PUT /api/contracts/{id}/events/{eventId}.summary: Replace one event on a contract (FULL replacement).
PUT /api/contracts/{id}/events/{eventId}.description:
null means "clear this field", NOT "leave unchanged" — the opposite of
                        PUT /api/contracts/{id}. A body omitting description or notes CLEARS it, and one
                        omitting type resets it to Other. createdBy and createdAtUtc are never rewritten
                        by an update. An event id that exists but belongs to a different contract is a
                        404, never a 403 and never a silent success.

PUT /api/contracts/{id}/files/{fileId}.summary: Update an attached document's type and validity metadata.
PUT /api/contracts/{id}/files/{fileId}.description: A full replacement: an omitted date or issuer clears the stored value. fileType may not be omitted. files.read is deliberately not required — this verb reads no file metadata and takes no file id the caller had not already attached.

PUT /api/contracts/{id}/parties/{partyId.summary: Re-write one party: its role, its target, its dates, or any combination (full replacement).

PUT /api/contracts/{id}/terms/{termId}.summary: Replace a term entry on a contract.
PUT /api/contracts/{id}/terms/{termId}.description:
The owner is not changeable through this endpoint — the route is the only
                        thing that names it. A term id belonging to a different contract is a 404, never a 403 and never a silent success.

                        This is a FULL replace and 'direction' is not exempt: omitting it resets the
                        term to Outgoing, exactly as omitting 'label', 'currencyCode', 'interval' or
                        'anchorDate' already clears those. That matters more here than elsewhere, since
                        it moves the amount from one side of the household's net to the other — read
                        the term back and send its direction with the replacement.

PUT /api/currencies/{code}.summary: Update the details for a currency.
PUT /api/currencies/{code}.description:
Update the details for a currency. Not an upsert: an unknown code is a 404 and
                        nothing is created. Use POST to create. Archiving a currency switches its
                        exchange-rate sync off, and restoring it does not switch it back on. Archiving
                        the sync's base currency while any currency is synced is a 422.

parameters.name: code
parameters.description: The code for the currency to update.

PUT /api/exchange-rates/{id}.description: Corrects the Rate and AsOf of an existing manual exchange rate record. The currency pair is the record's identity and can't be changed. A fetched rate is refused with 422 keyed source.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The ID of the exchange rate record to update.

PUT /api/files/{id}/metadata.description: Update metadata for a file (currently only description).

PUT /api/instrument-prices/{id}.summary: Correct a manual price's date and close. A fetched row is refused with 422 keyed source.

PUT /api/instruments/{id}.summary: Update an instrument. Not an upsert; identity fields are immutable once prices or sources exist.

PUT /api/journal-entries/{id}.summary: Update a journal entry and replace its tag, contact, photo and attachment links.

PUT /api/journal-tags/{id}.summary: Update a journal tag and toggle its archival state.

PUT /api/locations/{id}.summary: Replace a location; archived: true archives it, false restores it. Not an upsert.

PUT /api/locations/{id}/weather-point.summary: Link a location to a weather point, or clear the link with null.

PUT /api/news-articles/{id}/read-state.summary: Mark one article read or unread. Idempotent.

PUT /api/news-articles/{id}/tags/{tagId}.summary: Add one tag to an article. Idempotent; an archived tag is a 422.

PUT /api/news-feeds/{id}.summary: Replace a feed's settings under its version; a url equal to the pending suggestion accepts it.

PUT /api/news-feeds/{id}/tags.summary: Replace a feed's tags; every article of the feed inherits them.

PUT /api/news-tags/{id}.summary: Update a news tag and toggle its archival state.

PUT /api/photo-tags/{id}.summary: Update a photo tag and toggle its archival state.

PUT /api/photos/{id}.summary: Update a photo's metadata and replace its tag/person/album links; set/clear archive.

PUT /api/profile.summary: Set the current user's own profile (required fields must be present & valid).

PUT /api/properties/{id}.description:
Full replace; not an upsert. The type is fixed at creation: a body whose type
                        differs from the stored one is refused with 422.

PUT /api/properties/{propertyId}/estimat.summary: Update an estimated-value entry on a property.

PUT /api/properties/{propertyId}/events/.summary: Replace one event on a property (FULL replacement).
PUT /api/properties/{propertyId}/events/.description:
null means "clear this field", NOT "leave unchanged". A body omitting
                        description or notes CLEARS it, and one omitting type resets it to Other. A
                        system-only type may be kept on a row that already carries it, never introduced.
                        An event id belonging to another property or to a contract is a 404.

PUT /api/properties/{propertyId}/files/{.summary: Update an attached property document's type and validity metadata.
PUT /api/properties/{propertyId}/files/{.description:
A full replacement: an omitted date or issuer clears the stored value; fileType
                        may not be omitted. files.read is deliberately not required — this verb reads no
                        file metadata and takes no file id the caller had not already attached.

PUT /api/recipe-tags/{id}.summary: Update a recipe tag and toggle its archived state.

PUT /api/recipes/{id}.summary: Replace a recipe (not an upsert). A stale version is 409 recipe-version-conflict; photoIds / attachmentFileIds null leave those links unchanged.

PUT /api/recurrence-patterns/{id}.summary: Update a series' template, rule and zone; reconciles its future rows in place by occurrence key, keeping every override and exclusion whose key survives, and reports what it dropped.

PUT /api/system-settings/exchange-rate-s.summary: Turn sync on or off for one currency and set its start-date override.

PUT /api/system-settings/instrument-pric.summary: Replace an instrument's whole binding list; priority is position.

PUT /api/task-tags/{id}.summary: Rename, describe, or archive-toggle a task tag.

PUT /api/tasks/{id}.summary: Update a task's fields, links, lifecycle status and board position.

PUT /api/tax-statements/{id}.summary: Update a tax statement's declared figures, period, currency, dates and settlement.

PUT /api/tax-statements/{id}/tags.summary: Replace the selected tax-payment, income and settlement tag sets in one call.

PUT /api/transaction-tags/{id}.summary: Update the details for a transaction tag.
PUT /api/transaction-tags/{id}.description:
Update the details for a transaction tag. Not an upsert: an unknown ID is a 404 and
                        nothing is created. Use POST to create.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The ID for the transaction tag to update.

PUT /api/transactions/{id}.summary: Update the details for a transaction.
PUT /api/transactions/{id}.description:
Update the details for a transaction. Not an upsert: an unknown ID is a 404 and
                        nothing is created. Use POST to create.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The ID for the transaction to update.

PUT /api/user-preferences/{pageKey}.summary: Update user preference for page key.
PUT /api/user-preferences/{pageKey}.description: Update user preference for page key.

parameters.name: pageKey
parameters.description: The page key for the user preference to update.

PUT /api/weather/points/{weatherPointId}.summary: Change a weather point's settings; a changed position, altitude or time zone starts a new site. Not an upsert.

PUT /api/weather/preferences.summary: Set the caller's own weather place; null follows the household default.
